facts.claim: retail dispensary licenses in the five boroughs
facts.source_name: New York State Office of Cannabis Management, Current OCM Licenses (data.ny.gov)
facts.verify: Socrata: $select=city,count(*) filtered to license_type like '%Retail Dispensary%', grouped by city. Manhattan appears as city value 'New York'. QUEENS RESOLVED 2026-08-10: OCM records Queens addresses under 35 separate neighborhood values (Jamaica 14, Flushing 13, Long Island City 11, Astoria 10, Ridgewood 6, Rosedale 6, and 29 more), summing to 128. Any Queens figure must aggregate those, never read a single 'Queens' row.

facts.claim: tax on adult-use cannabis at retail
facts.source_name: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance, adult-use cannabis products tax
facts.verify: 9 percent state plus 4 percent local, the local share staying with the city, town, village, or county where the sale occurs

facts.claim: the per-milligram THC potency tax was replaced by a 9 percent distributor tax
facts.source_name: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance, historical adult-use cannabis rates
facts.verify: Before 2024-06-01 the tax ran on milligrams of total THC (0.5 cents per mg flower, 0.8 concentrate, 3 cents edibles). From that date a 9 percent distributor tax applies instead.
facts.note: Any content still describing NY cannabis tax in cents per milligram is more than two years out of date.

facts.claim: retail dispensary licenses that are operationally active, versus issued
facts.source_name: New York State Office of Cannabis Management, Current OCM Licenses (data.ny.gov)
facts.verify: The dataset carries an operational_status field with values Active and Non-Operational. Filter license_type like '%Retail Dispensary%' and group by operational_status. Queens requires summing its 35 neighborhood city values.
facts.note: Resolves the licenses-versus-open-stores gap. Statewide 638 of 1,115 retail licenses are Active. Borough active share: Manhattan 67 percent, Brooklyn 57, Staten Island 52, Bronx 51, Queens 55. Roughly four in ten licensed NYC dispensaries are not trading.

gaps: Legalization and first-sale dates: MRTA (2021) and the first legal sale (late 2022) both need primary citations.
